posts.author: MichaelH
posts.content_md:
I've gone as short as 30 minutes drying when using a light-tight box with dessicant to speed things up.

Definitely use it within a day or put it into the fridge for longer storage. TEA will cause increasing degradation of at least PFG-01 over longer periods.

posts.author: Tom B.
posts.content_md:
1) TEA generally increases film sensitivity by a factor of 2 or more. You should re-check your exposure to avoid overexposure which can lead to milkiness.

2) A more subtle problem which I rarely see mentioned is that even if both sides are squeegeed, TEA leaves a hazy film on the glass (or non-emusion side of the film) which shows up as diffuse milkiness in the hologram. The cure is to wipe the non-emulsion side with a clean wet paper towel and then gently wipe dry with a dry cloth. You can see the hazy scum by reflection in a safelight and it is easy to see when the plate has been cleared.

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md: When hair drying I use a low heat and bounce a safe light off the emulsion side. As the "shine" leaves the first section I chace it off the film. However milky is not a problem I have experienced.

posts.author: MichaelH
posts.content_md:
Do you have a digital camera? A picture might help us diagnose this faster.

Have you tried cutting your development time in half? TEA "speeds" up the film so you either need to reduce the exposure time or reduce the development time. Ideally you'd do the former but the latter will get you similar results.

Without seeing a picture I'm inclined to think that the film is over exposed/developed which can cause a milkyness with some films after bleaching.

posts.author: John Sonley
posts.content_md:
As a fairly new experimenter in TEA pre-swelling I submit 2 ideas:

1) Are you using distilled or de-ionised water in all your final washes - chlorides can be bad news

2) May be worthwhile distilled/deionised water washing the unexposed film for 2 minutes before TEA treatment - I am told that some films have preservatives that need to be removed prior to swelling 

Otherwise, I do just as you and no cloudiness on my old AGFA film, which is now 20 years old but is still working fine!

BRgds

John
